title: Written Exposure Therapy Plus Adjunctive Methylphenidate Treatment for Veterans With PTSD
official: Enhancing Written Exposure Therapy in Veterans With Posttraumatic Stress: Clinical, Physiological and Behavioral Markers of Adjunctive Methylphenidate Treatment
summary: Many Veterans with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) do not fully benefit from the best current treatments, some of which focus on helping the brain regulate trauma memories. While therapies like Prolonged Exposure and Written Exposure Therapy work for many, about half of Veterans still struggle with symptoms even after treatment. Research suggests that methylphenidate (commonly known as Ritalin), a safe and widely used medication, may improve PTSD symptoms and related mechanisms. This project will test whether adding methylphenidate to Written Exposure Therapy will result in a greater reduction in PTSD symptoms compared to Written Exposure Therapy alone. The investigators will also study body and behavior markers to better understand how and why some Veterans respond to treatment. If successful, this approach could give providers a new, practical tool to improve recovery from PTSD. Ultimately, this work could lead to more personalized, effective care for Veterans, helping them return to fuller and healthier lives.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Veteran
2. Current post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms
3. Medically healthy
4. Body weight of ≥ 120 pounds (55 kilograms)
5. Participants must be able to participate and willing to give written informed consent and to comply with the study restrictions

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Major medical issues
2. Medical conditions that could alter the absorption, metabolism or elimination of study drug
3. Family history of sudden death or ventricular arrhythmia
4. History of glaucoma
5. History, including family history, of motor tic or diagnosis of Tourette's syndrome
6. Pregnancy or lactation
7. Lifetime history of a chronic psychotic disorder or bipolar disorder type I
8. Lifetime history of stimulant use disorder
9. Current moderate or severe substance use disorder for any other substances
10. High suicidal risk
11. Marked anxiety, tension, or agitation, based on clinical observation, that is not due to an outside identifiable, transient, or modifiable cause
12. Unable to abstain from alcohol the evening before or day of study drug administration
13. History of a traumatic brain injury (TBI) resulting in loss of consciousness for more than 30 minutes
14. Drugs of abuse as determined by a positive urine test, excepting THC
15. Current use of any psychotropic medication that has not been at a stable dose
16. Current or recent use of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor or any other medication deemed by the study physician to exhibit an unsafe interaction with methylphenidate (MPH)
17. Past intolerance to methylphenidate (MPH) or any other psychostimulant
18. Current uncontrolled hypertension
19. Current heavy smoker and/or heavy caffeine consumption and unable to limit on study days
20. Abnormal Electrocardiogram, per study physician
21. Participation in a clinical trial with an investigational drug or a device within 30 days prior to dosing.
22. Concurrent participation in an evidence-based behavioral therapy treatment for PTSD
23. Volunteers who are unable to understand the informed consent form(s) and complete the study procedures including clinical testing
24. Any other reason, per study investigators, that would put the participant at undue risk or interfere with the conduct of the study per protocol
